title: Prayer for the Beauty of a Young Woman
text:
You gave her that burning symmetry

of the lips, with an ember from your depth,

and in two enormous channels of blackness,

chasms of infinity, the light of your day;


those masses of snow, which stirred

when the smoothness of linen was lifted,

and, wonders of exact architecture,

two columns that sing your harmony.


Ah, you, Lord, gave her that slope

that pours down in a gentle curve,

secret honey in the gold-threaded smoke.


What is your powerful hand waiting for?

Mortal beauty demands eternity.

Give her the eternity you have denied her!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the sonnet as a prayer that turns physical beauty into a demand for eternity.

title: Love
text:
Fierce spring! My tenderness goes

spilled through the deepest veins,

fresh fountainhead, and wakeful fury,

hurrying toward exhausting amazement.


Oh what panting, what boiling, oh, what haste

to find, in the closed hill,

the red wound of the frozen cave,

and its sweetest cure, in madness!


Fleeting monster, terror of my life,

lightless lightning, oh you, my spring,

my fierce beast, my strong archangel!


Toward what shadowy depth does your hair,

unfurled and astral, invite me?

Love, love, beginning of death!
editorial_note: The translation keeps love as both spring-force and deathward terror, preserving the poem's erotic and apocalyptic force.

title: Imminent Destruction
text:
Shall I break you, little hazel wand,

shall I perhaps break you? Oh tender life,

blind passion born in green boiling,

you, fragile being I press in my hand!


A fleeting spark, only a light

crack in sweet shuddering pulp,

and you will learn, oh helpless branch,

how much death could do in a summer.


But no; I will leave you... Play in the wind

until, in sharp autumn, you lose

your green frenzy, leaf by leaf.


Give me autumn too, Lord, for I feel

I know not what deep cracking, what mute terror.

Hold back, oh God, your red blaze.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the threatened twig as a figure for mortality and asks God to delay the destructive flame.

title: Women
text:
Oh, whiteness. Who placed in our lives,

lives of frantic abyssal beasts,

this brightness of sidereal lights,

these snows, inflamed with dream?


Oh sweet little pursued beasts.

Oh smooth touch. Oh zenithal signs.

Oh musics. Oh flames. Oh crystals.

Oh tall sails, risen from the sea.


Ah, timid gleams, pure dawn,

who brought you to this hard man's chest,

to this black uproar of hatred and forgetting?


Sweet specters, clouds, vain flowers...

Oh tender shadows, vaguely human,

sad women, made of air or of moan!
editorial_note: The translation preserves the historical diction and the poem's movement from celestial whiteness to ghostly human sorrow.

title: How Beautiful You Are, Freedom. There Is Nothing...
text:
How beautiful you are, freedom. There is nothing

to set against you. What? Give me torment.

Freedom, refined in torment,

shines brighter in a purer firmament.


Not cry out? Is a gag prepared?

Come: gag my thought.

A cry is not the vibration of waves in the wind:

a cry is the conscience of a man in revolt.


How beautiful you are, freedom. God himself

saw you shine, before the first abyss,

upon his breast, a solitary star.


A little spark from the burning volcano

he took in his hand. And he lit you on my forehead,

free flame of God, beautiful freedom.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the hymn-like address to freedom and the distinction between sound and rebellious conscience.
